description: JAGANTRA is a solo team focused on exploring space and innovation through aerospace knowledge, software, storytelling, and creative digital solutions.
summary:
The Relics of Space is an interactive scrollytelling web app built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It maps and preserves humanity's historical footprints on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space.

Guided by Zog, a two-eyed extraterrestrial narrator, the platform transforms scattered NASA NSSDCA archives into an engaging 3D digital museum across three cosmic realms. From the Apollo 11 Lunar Module to interstellar probes like Voyager 1, it pairs 12 verified NASA space relics with detailed technical specs, authentic media, and a complete chronological timeline spanning 1957 to 2026.

By bridging open-access NASA datasets with character-driven visual storytelling, The Relics of Space helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts explore what we have left behind. It highlights why preserving space history matters for safe and sustainable future exploration.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

The Relics of Space is an interactive scrollytelling web app that preserves humanity's artifacts on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space. Guided by Zog, a friendly two-eyed alien narrator, users scroll through three cosmic realms and a 3D digital museum of 12 verified NASA relics. Each relic comes with a spacecraft model, a technical spec card (NSSDCA ID, launch or landing date, mass, and how it operates), and authentic NASA media. An interactive timeline (1957-2026) places every relic within nearly 70 years of spaceflight history.

BENEFITS

- Centralizes open NASA data: turns scattered NSSDCA and planetary archive records into one easy portal.

- Makes learning fun: narrative storytelling makes space history and orbital mechanics accessible to learners of all ages.

- Builds preservation awareness: documenting off-world artifacts encourages appreciation of space heritage as humanity becomes multiplanetary.

INTENDED IMPACT

The project bridges open NASA databases and public engagement. By showing the physical footprint we have left behind, it inspires students, educators, and space enthusiasts to support sustainable, responsible exploration in the Artemis era and beyond.

TOOLS USED

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), React.js, Tailwind CSS, , and Visual Studio Code. Data sources: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS), and NASA Planetary Data System (PDS).

CREATIVITY

Instead of a static table of spacecraft, we turn data exploration into an emotional journey. Zog, an alien historian visiting human "cosmic ruins," shows our technology through fresh, curious eyes. Parallax scrolling, color shifts across realms, and interactive spec cards bring cold, abandoned metal back to life.

KEY CONSIDERATIONS

- Data accuracy: every NSSDCA ID, mass, landing coordinate, and timeline event was checked against official NASA sources, with proper attribution.

- Accessibility and performance: 3D assets and animations are optimized for smooth performance on browsers and mobile screens.

- Scalability: the data structure lets us easily add new missions, commercial landers, and future deep-space probes.
